title: airgap kms-provisioner and certificate pinning for offline upgrade flows
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Context and motivation: Customers performing air-gapped or temporarily-offline Private deployments asked for a safer, auditable way to provision KMS keys and perform TLS upgrades when the cluster cannot reach Redwood control-plane during upgrade windows. Existing approaches require live connectivity for key wrap/unwrap or rely on operator-driven key promotion which is fragile in constrained networking conditions. This PR introduces an offline-first KMS Provisioner and a cert-pinning mechanism to make staged offline upgrades predictable and rollback-safe.

What this PR delivers (top-level):
- A new Kubernetes operator (airgap-kms-provisioner) that can accept an envelope-wrapped key blob delivered via secure media or an airgap artifact registry and atomically provision it into supported KMS backends (HSM, Vault transit, or local sealed keystore).
- A Helm values profile and templates to install the provisioner in airgap mode (charts/redwood-private/templates/airgap-kms-provisioner.yaml + charts/redwood-private/values-airgap.yaml).
- A Terraform module for pre-staging key artifacts into customer-controlled object stores and validating integrity checksums (terraform/modules/airgap-kms-provisioner).
- Certificate pinning support: installer option to inject trusted leaf or CA fingerprints into the cluster (config/cert-pinning-configmap and installer/scripts/offline-cert-pinning.sh) and a runtime check in the provisioner that enforces the pinned chain during upgrade/validation.
- Migration/upgrade tooling: a safe staged activation flag (provisioner.stagedActivation=true) that performs a dry-run verify, a canary apply to a single control-plane node, and an automatic rollback window if health checks fail.
- End-to-end tests that simulate disconnected upgrades and key provisioning using a local test harness (tests/e2e/airgap_kms_provisioner_test.go).

Design notes and security considerations:
- Envelope format: hybrid design using RSA-OAEP for the envelope key and AES-GCM for the wrapped symmetric key to minimize attack surface during transfer. The operator only ever stores wrapped blobs in sealed Kubernetes secrets; unwrap only occurs inside an ephemeral memory buffer with immediate zeroing.
- No implicit internet dependency: artifact verification uses SHA-512 checksums signed by an organizational signing key; Terraform module offers an optional key signing step so customers can verify artifacts out-of-band.
- Rollback safety: stagedActivation flag ensures we can verify health probes before activating new keys; activation is implemented as an atomic label flip on a dedicated KMS binding CRD and recorded in an audit annotation for easy revert.
- Auditability: operator writes structured audit events to the cluster audit sink and emits Prometheus metrics (kms_provisioner_provision_total, kms_provisioner_failures_total) exposed to the Redwood Console when connected.

Migration and rollback instructions (short):
- Pre-stage: run terraform module to upload envelope blobs to customer object store and record signed checksums.
- Install: helm install --values values-airgap.yaml charts/redwood-private --set provisioner.enabled=true --set provisioner.stagedActivation=true
- Validate: operator reports readiness=false while dry-run completes. Verify check-sum audit annotations and test KMS unwrap on a single canary node.
- Activate: flip provisioner.stagedActivation=false via kubectl patch; health checks run and if any fail within the window operator rolls back to previous binding and emits a kms_provisioner_activation_failed metric.
